workflow.role:
You are the deployment specialist responsible for orchestrating the ship phase. Your responsibilities: 1. Gather comprehensive context about the PR and changes 2. Perform pre-flight analysis to assess deployment risk 3. Generate release notes when appropriate 4. Make the go/no-go merge decision based on risk assessment 5. Produce a structured ship report with status markers
NOTE: Deploy commands (version_bump, build, publish) are executed deterministically by post.sh — NOT by the LLM.

step.critical: Collect all necessary context before making any decisions

substep.name: gather-pr-info
substep.action: Execute via Bash: ```bash gh pr view --json number,title,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup ```

Parse JSON output and store: - {{pr_number}} - The PR number - {{pr_title}} - The PR title - {{mergeable}} - Boolean indicating if PR can be merged - {{merge_state_status}} - CLEAN, BLOCKED, BEHIND, DIRTY, HAS_HOOKS, UNKNOWN - {{review_decision}} - APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, REVIEW_REQUIRED, null - {{status_checks}} - Array of check statuses

check.action: Note: "PR information unavailable - proceeding with limited context"

substep.name: detect-version
substep.critical: Version detection follows priority order: package.json → pyproject.toml → Cargo.toml → VERSION
substep.action: Check for version files in order:

check.if: package.json does NOT exist AND pyproject.toml exists
check.action: Extract version from: - [project].version (PEP 621 standard) - OR [tool.poetry].version (Poetry projects)

check.if: package.json and pyproject.toml do NOT exist AND Cargo.toml exists
none of above exist AND VERSION file exists

check.note: No version file detected - version bump will be skipped

substep.name: gather-git-history
substep.action: Execute via Bash: ```bash git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "no-tags" ```
Store result as {{last_tag}}

check.note: No tags found - showing recent commits only

substep.name: extract-ship-config
substep.action: Extract ship configuration from project config (provided in context): - {{version_bump_command}} - Command to bump version (if configured) - {{build_command}} - Command to build (if configured) - {{publish_command}} - Command to publish (if configured) - {{merge_on_success}} - Whether to auto-merge on success - {{merge_method}} - merge, squash, or rebase - {{delete_branch}} - Whether to delete branch after merge

substep.name: display-context
analyze-breaking-changes
substep.action: Analyze {{commit_list}} for breaking change indicators: - Commits with "BREAKING CHANGE:" in body - Commits with "!" after type (e.g., "feat!:", "fix!:", "refactor!:") - Commits containing "BREAKING:" prefix - Keywords: "breaking", "migration required", "schema change"
Store findings as {{breaking_changes}} list
Set {{has_breaking_changes}} = true if any found

substep.name: analyze-security
substep.action: Check if changes include security-sensitive files: - Authentication/authorization code (auth/, security/, login, session) - Environment files (.env*, secrets, credentials) - Cryptographic code (crypto, encrypt, decrypt, hash) - Permission/access control changes - New dependencies in lock files
Execute via Bash to get changed files: ```bash git diff {{last_tag}}..HEAD --name-only 2>/dev/null || git diff HEAD~{{commit_count}}..HEAD --name-only ```
Store security-sensitive files as {{security_files}}
Set {{has_security_changes}} = true if any found

substep.name: evaluate-pr-readiness
substep.action: Evaluate PR merge readiness based on gathered context:

check.action: Add to {{blocking_issues}}: "PR is blocked by branch protection rules"
Add to {{warnings}}: "PR branch is behind base branch"
Add to {{blocking_issues}}: "PR has changes requested by reviewers"

check.if: any status check in {{status_checks}} has state 'FAILURE' or 'ERROR'
check.action: Add to {{blocking_issues}}: "Required status checks are failing"

check.if: {{has_breaking_changes}} == false AND {{has_security_changes}} == false AND {{review_decision}} == 'APPROVED' AND {{merge_state_status}} == 'CLEAN' AND {{blocking_issues}} is empty
check.action: Set {{risk_justification}} = "No breaking changes, no security modifications, PR approved and mergeable, all checks passing"

check.if: ({{has_breaking_changes}} == true AND breaking changes have migration path documented) OR ({{has_security_changes}} == true AND changes are to non-critical security components) OR ({{merge_state_status}} == 'CLEAN' AND {{review_decision}} != 'APPROVED')
check.action: Set {{risk_justification}} based on specific conditions met

check.if: ({{has_breaking_changes}} == true AND no migration path documented) OR (security changes affect core auth/security systems) OR ({{blocking_issues}} is not empty)
check.action: Set {{risk_justification}} based on specific conditions met

substep.critical: BLOCKED status is definitive and prevents all deployment actions

check.action: Skip remaining steps - jump to report generation

substep.action: Get current date in YYYY-MM-DD format

substep.name: categorize-commits
substep.critical: Parse each commit from {{commit_list}} and categorize by conventional commit prefix
substep.action: Initialize empty category lists: - {{commits_added}} = [] - {{commits_changed}} = [] - {{commits_fixed}} = [] - {{commits_documentation}} = [] - {{commits_other}} = []
For each commit in {{commit_list}}:

check.if: commit message does NOT match any conventional commit prefix pattern

substep.name: clean-commit-messages
substep.critical: Clean each commit message for human-readable release notes
substep.action: For each categorized commit, apply cleaning rules:
Rule 1: Remove conventional commit prefix - "feat: add authentication" → "add authentication" - "feat(api): new endpoint" → "new endpoint" - "fix!: breaking change" → "breaking change"
Rule 2: Remove scope if present - "(api)" → removed - "(core)" → removed
Rule 3: Capitalize first letter - "add authentication" → "Add authentication"
Rule 4: Remove trailing punctuation if present - "Add authentication." → "Add authentication"
Rule 5: Use first line only for multi-line commits - Keep only the first line (before any newline)
Rule 6: Deduplicate messages - If squash commits include original messages, keep unique entries only

substep.name: generate-changelog-format
substep.critical: Format release notes following Keep a Changelog specification
substep.action: Initialize {{release_notes_content}} with header: ```markdown ## [{{release_version}}] - {{release_date}} ```
substep.note: Empty sections are omitted from output
